title: Weeknote #2023
summary: I started on a project I have no idea how to do, museums, and a random smattering of other things
content:
I've started work on a card game and I have no idea what I'm doing so if anyone has any good articles to check out, send them my way.

I was personally attacked at the weekend while driving through Basingstoke and saw a sign for a museum exhibit entitled "I Grew Up 90s". Given the 90s were only 10 years ago[1], this seems premature.

DNS Museum is a reference for the odd, inventive, and always impractical things people have done with DNS. Maths over DNS anyone?.

Speaking of DNS, Record Relay is an experiment to see how long a chain can be made with TXT records. I'm number two. And a few others.

Sophie wrote a great post about storing recipes including this incredible line "originally storing them in Evernote, which is what we did in the 2010s". Remember Evernote? I'm trying out Mealie at the moment and I like that it costs me nothing but I could make my life easier with a more advanced app like Paprika.

I tooted at Dan because we were both listening to Ms Rachel's album and he posted back this eldritch horror of an image featuring me, him, and Ry.

Keenan wrote a great post[2] about their adventures moving to Poland and buying lemons, among other things.

I really like this analog defaults post.

XKCD was on point on Wednesday morning.

This is my favourite Inktober I've done so far.

Everhand is a handwriting font that has three versions of every letter so no two letters are the same next to each other. Incredible stuff.

  1. Shut up. ⤾

  2. All their posts are great, talented git ⤾
